fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.topology_type: Two-wire host-to-target serial debug bus (no daisy chain). The host drives SWCLK; SWDIO is bidirectional with explicit Turnaround periods. Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2) shares SWDIO/SWCLK across multiple targets in parallel with per-target selection via TARGETSEL.

supported_topologies.name: Single-target SWD
supported_topologies.description: One debug host + one target SoC. 2 pins (SWCLK + SWDIO) between them. Most common configuration.

supported_topologies.name: SWJ-DP mode-switched
supported_topologies.description: Single target supports both SWD and JTAG via the same physical pads (SWCLK=TCK, SWDIO=TMS); mode is selected at runtime by 16-bit selection sequences.

supported_topologies.name: Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2)
supported_topologies.description: Multiple targets share SWDIO/SWCLK in parallel; per-target selection via DP TARGETSEL after line reset + JTAG-to-SWD sequence.

supported_topologies.name: SWD + SWO trace
supported_topologies.description: Single target with the dedicated SWO trace pin providing ITM/DWT trace output (separate from SWD protocol).

supported_topologies.name: ARM 10-pin Cortex Debug header
supported_topologies.description: Standard 10-pin Arm Cortex Debug connector — carries SWCLK + SWDIO + GND + VTREF + RESET. Compact alternative to the older 20-pin JTAG ITAG/CoreSight header.

supported_topologies.name: ARM 20-pin Cortex+ETM header
supported_topologies.description: 20-pin connector that adds 4-bit parallel trace data (TRACEDATA[3:0] + TRACECLK) on top of SWCLK + SWDIO for high-bandwidth ETM trace capture.

supported_topologies.name: TC2050 / Tag-Connect
supported_topologies.description: Compact production needle-probe footprint — no PCB connector required; the debug probe plugs into a 6-pin pad pattern.

master_slave_role_summary.description: USB-to-SWD probe (J-Link, ST-Link, CMSIS-DAP, Black Magic Probe, ULINK, PE Micro, etc.). Drives SWCLK; bidirectionally drives or tri-states SWDIO. Sequences 46-bit transactions, manages DP.SELECT for AP banking, recovers posted reads via RDBUFF.
Arm Cortex-based SoC implementing SW-DP / SWJ-DP wire-level + DP register set + one or more APs (MEM-AP variants, JTAG-AP). Decodes Request, drives ACK and Read-Data, samples Write-Data.
ADIv5.2 — additional SoCs sharing SWDIO/SWCLK; each has a unique TARGETID.TPARTNO + DLPIDR.TINSTANCE; selected via TARGETSEL.
External authentication interface (DBGEN / NIDEN / SPIDEN / SPNIDEN) that gates the DAP — optional, vendor-specific; not part of ADIv5 base spec.

fields.interconnect_role: There is NO daisy chain at the SWD wire layer (unlike JTAG). SWD is a point-to-point bus between host and target (or multi-drop in ADIv5.2). On the target side, the DAP internally fans transactions out to up to 256 APs over an internal AP bus; each AP can be a MEM-AP (bridging to AHB/AXI/APB) or a JTAG-AP (forwarding to a downstream JTAG TAP chain — this is how SWD can reach legacy JTAG IP without the host needing to switch to JTAG mode).

ordering_guarantees.bit_order_within_a_phase: Bits transmitted LSB-first on SWDIO; receiver reassembles LSB-first.
ordering_guarantees.transaction_order: Strict sequential — each 46-bit transaction completes before the next begins. Posted reads pipeline the data return, but the wire-level ordering of transactions is strict.
ordering_guarantees.posted_read_pipelining: AP read N's data appears with the ACK of transaction N+1 (or RDBUFF). Hosts must track the pipeline depth.
ordering_guarantees.ap_register_atomicity: Each AP register read/write is atomic from the host's POV; the AP layer's internal handshake to the system bus is hidden behind ACK=OK/WAIT/FAULT and CSW.TrInProg.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: DP registers are accessed via APnDP=0 + A[3:2] addressing — not memory-mapped. AP registers are accessed via APnDP=1 + SELECT.APSEL + APBANKSEL + A[3:2]. MEM-AP register CSW + TAR + DRW provides a window into the SoC's memory-mapped system bus (any AHB/AXI/APB address reachable by the bus master role).

device_classification.debug_host: USB-to-SWD/JTAG probe — drives the wire-level interface from outside the SoC.
device_classification.swd_only_target: SoC with SW-DP only (no JTAG capability) — typical resource-constrained Cortex-M0+ MCU.
device_classification.swj_dp_target: SoC with SWJ-DP — supports both SWD and JTAG modes on the same pads.
device_classification.multi_drop_target: SoC with DLPIDR (ADIv5.2) — can share an SWD bus with other multi-drop targets.
device_classification.non_dap_ic: IC without an ADIv5 DAP — not debuggable via SWD; may be reachable via JTAG-AP if downstream JTAG TAP is implemented.
